public_rationale: OpenAI documented plausible mistakes in the relevant period. Earlier benchmarks also showed meaningful factual competence. Neither finding settles whether contemporary GPT reliably distinguished appropriate entity-property combinations across ordinary contexts. Scoring this as supported would turn occasional errors into a general incapacity; scoring it as contradicted would turn limited benchmark success into broad reliability.
limitations: Generation accuracy, factual recall and relational discrimination are different abilities.
Earlier evaluations cannot automatically be assigned to the launch-period system.
The meaning of know materially affects the assessment.

public_payload.normalized_proposition: GPT does not know which entities properly go with which properties.

statement.excerpt: GPT doesn’t actually know which of the elements appropriately combine with which other properties.
statement.document_title: How come GPT can seem so brilliant one minute and so breathtakingly dumb the next?

from_speaker: which of the elements appropriately combine
our_interpretation: Know is assessed behaviorally: reliably distinguishing appropriate entity-property combinations from plausible but inappropriate ones.
The surrounding discussion acknowledges successful outputs, so the claim is not read as saying GPT never makes a correct association.
The full post discusses failures during the preceding 24 hours. The observation period is the current public snapshot from November 30 through December 1, 2022.
The relevant systems are the GPT-3 generation and launch-era ChatGPT, not later models.
criteria.support_condition: Controlled evaluations of the relevant systems demonstrate substantial, systematic failures to distinguish valid from invalid entity-property combinations across ordinary contexts.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Controlled evaluations demonstrate robust discrimination across ordinary contexts, including unfamiliar combinations and plausible distractors.

evidence.explanation: This supports the narrower observation that launch-era ChatGPT could produce plausible mistakes. It does not establish a general inability to distinguish appropriate entity-property combinations.

evidence.publisher: Stanford Center for Research on Foundation Models / arXiv
evidence.explanation: These earlier evaluations show meaningful factual competence in an instruction-tuned GPT model, qualifying an absolute absence-of-knowledge reading. They do not establish broad relational reliability or measure the exact launch-period ChatGPT snapshot.

public_payload.what_would_resolve: A controlled evaluation of the relevant 2022 model snapshots using matched entity-property combinations, varied wording and plausible distractors, with a justified reliability standard.
